name: Sri Lanka
genZNote: One island, two official languages, ancient stupas older than most empires — Sri Lanka's history didn't wait for anyone else's timeline.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: An island nation in the Indian Ocean, just southeast of India across the Palk Strait/Gulf of Mannar.
Central highlands with tea-growing hill country; coastal plains ring the island.
Official capital: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte (seat of Parliament); Colombo is the commercial capital and largest city.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Sinhala and Tamil are the two official languages; the population is majority Sinhalese-Buddhist, with significant Tamil-Hindu, Muslim, and Christian communities.
Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa, ancient royal capitals, are UNESCO World Heritage Sites with well-preserved Buddhist stupas and ruins.
The Sigiriya rock fortress is another major UNESCO-listed heritage site.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A unitary semi-presidential republic; the President is both head of state and head of government, alongside a Prime Minister and unicameral Parliament.
Independence from British rule in 1948; was known as Ceylon until renamed Sri Lanka in 1972.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: Member of the United Nations, SAARC, and the Commonwealth of Nations.
Strategically positioned along major Indian Ocean shipping lanes, making it a focus of regional maritime and infrastructure interest.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Sri Lanka share close cultural and religious ties, particularly through Buddhism and Tamil linguistic connections with Tamil Nadu.
India has provided significant economic and development assistance to Sri Lanka, including support during Sri Lanka's 2022 economic crisis.
The Palk Strait fishing-rights issue is a recurring bilateral topic between the two countries' coastal communities.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: Tea (Ceylon Tea), textiles/garments, and tourism are major economic sectors.
The Port of Colombo is a key transshipment hub in the Indian Ocean.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Ceylon Tea, ancient Buddhist heritage sites (Anuradhapura, Polonnaruwa, Sigiriya), and Indian Ocean maritime trade significance.

sections.heading: 💰 Currency & Economy
bullets: Currency: Sri Lankan Rupee (LKR).
Economy historically centred on tea, garments, and tourism; experienced a severe economic and debt crisis in 2022.

sections.heading: 🌿 Ecology & Environment
bullets: Exceptional biodiversity for its size, including rainforests, and is a globally recognised biodiversity hotspot.
Home to significant Asian elephant and leopard populations; Sinharaja Forest Reserve is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sections.heading: 📜 History & Major Turning Points
bullets: Home to ancient Sinhalese kingdoms with a Buddhist heritage dating back over two millennia.
Colonized successively by the Portuguese, Dutch, and British; gained independence from Britain in 1948.
Endured a prolonged civil war (1983-2009) between the government and Tamil separatist forces.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Major Political & Constitutional Changes
bullets: 1948 independence from Britain.
The 1972 and 1978 Constitutions reshaped governance, with the latter introducing an executive presidency; the 2009 end of the civil war marked a major turning point.

sections.heading: 🏅 Sports, Arts & Global Recognition
bullets: Cricket is the most popular sport; Sri Lanka won the Cricket World Cup in 1996.
Ancient cities Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa, along with Sigiriya rock fortress, are UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
Ceylon tea remains a globally recognised export brand.

sections.heading: 🌐 International Organizations & Important Memberships
bullets: Founding member of SAARC and the Non-Aligned Movement.
Member of the UN and the Commonwealth of Nations.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Sri Lanka is an island nation off India's southeastern coast, a unitary semi-presidential republic known for ancient Buddhist heritage and tea exports.
keyFacts: Official capital: Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte. Commercial capital: Colombo. Currency: Sri Lankan Rupee.
Independence from Britain: 1948. Renamed from Ceylon to Sri Lanka: 1972.
commonConfusion: Sri Lanka's official (Kotte) and commercial (Colombo) capitals are different cities — a frequently tested distinction.

highYieldFacts: Was known as Ceylon until renamed Sri Lanka in 1972.
Two official languages: Sinhala and Tamil.
commonTraps: Naming Colombo as THE capital without noting it's the commercial capital, while Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte is the official/administrative one.
mustRemember: Sri Lanka = former Ceylon, island neighbour of India, independent since 1948.
